resolved: Each link flips independently with probability \(p\).
The ordinary syndrome is the incident-error parity at each available vertex.
Every vertex with at least two incident error bonds carries an independent herald with probability \(q\); odd-degree vertices also carry syndrome.

Stage 1 is executed by scripts/local_decoder.py in the order distance-one herald pairs, syndrome-herald-syndrome, then distance-two herald pairs; each rule uses a synchronous snapshot and consumes touched heralds only at that rule boundary.
Stage 2 discards all remaining heralds, builds a sparse detector-by-edge check matrix, and delegates the residual-syndrome correction to PyMatching.
Square and honeycomb use top/bottom smooth boundaries and left/right open rough plaquettes; the outward rough-side edge is absent and its outer vertices have no stabilizer.
The Results view rotates both lattices by 90 degrees, so rough boundaries appear at the top and bottom; boundary labels and thick guides are omitted.
Retained edges joining an open-side vertex to an interior detector become singleton check-matrix columns.
Logical error is the parity of displayed residual edges crossed by a dashed smooth-to-smooth path through the right open-plaquette centers.
The viewer reports error, syndrome, and visible-herald densities for its current decoder stage.

On the honeycomb lattice, \(d=0,1,2,3\) maps to noiseless messages none, parity, herald-eligible, and parity plus herald-eligible; the present baseline sets both measurement-error parameters \(p_m=p_h=0\).
Posterior inference, belief propagation, decoder benchmarking, and exact-oracle comparisons are owned by Lab 002.
